name: Adaptive Research (orchestrator-driven)
description: An ORCHESTRATED workflow: no fixed DAG. After each step, the orchestrator brain reads the goal + results so far and decides the next step to run — scoping, researching, drilling deeper only where needed, then writing up — or declares DONE when the goal is met. The path adapts to what comes back.
goal: Produce a well-supported, decision-ready brief answering: {{question}}

steps.title: Scope the question
steps.description: Break "{{question}}" into the 3-5 sub-questions that must be answered to reach a confident conclusion. List what evidence each needs. Output as markdown.

steps.title: Broad survey
steps.description: Do a broad first-pass survey of "{{question}}": the main perspectives, the current consensus, and where the biggest uncertainty is. Output as markdown.

steps.title: Deep dive on the crux
steps.description: Take the single most decision-critical uncertainty surfaced so far about "{{question}}" and investigate it in depth: mechanisms, evidence for and against, and what would change the answer. Output as markdown.

steps.title: Steelman the opposing view
steps.description: Argue the strongest case AGAINST the leading conclusion emerging about "{{question}}". Identify the assumptions it depends on and how robust they are. Output as markdown.

steps.title: Quantify / model
steps.description: Where the answer to "{{question}}" hinges on numbers, build a simple back-of-envelope model or estimate with stated assumptions and a sensitivity note. Output as markdown.

steps.title: Write the decision brief
steps.description: Synthesize everything gathered so far into a one-page, decision-ready brief on "{{question}}": the answer, the key supporting evidence, the main risk to being wrong, and a clear recommendation. Output as markdown.
